_comment: The kinds of part on a shop's shelves (see docs/modding.md, "part_groups.json"). A part is in the first group with
a class its script descends from, by the end of the class's name ("Block" takes in Block_Vee_OHV), the groups in
the order listed; a part no group takes in is an accessory. A mod's part_groups.json adds groups (tried before these)
or changes one of these by its id, naming only what it changes. The player reads part_group.<id> in the text, else
the group's name. never_stacks: never mounts on its own kind (a head on a head); bolt_on: what the cars on the lots
were worked on with; tune: how much a rival's tuner goes for it (10 the most, none: not at all); speed_shop: a speed
shop sells it. The ids engine_blocks to shocks below are the game's own: the engine's internals wear and break, the
running gear has a slot on each wheel. price: what a part of the kind costs new, in the game's dollars: base, and per_hp for
every horsepower the part is worth on the dyno (a block its engine's power, any other part what it makes over the
poorest of its kind in its place), the horsepower raised to hp_power first (none: 1); by a figure of its own (grip, brake_torque, rim_size, spring_rate, damping, carb_mounts) it
costs as much more or less as its figure stands against the middle one of its kind, to the power by_power (carb_mounts:
the carburettors a manifold takes: a kit no dyno run of the manifold alone measures). The
accessories group takes no classes: it prices the parts no group takes in.
shows: the parts view's buttons that put kinds of part out of sight, as the source game had them. Each names its
groups (the first that names a part's group takes it); rest_of_engine takes every other part of the engine; a part
no show takes stays in sight. The player reads part_show.<id> as the button's tooltip. A mod adds shows, or changes
one by its id. The drivetrain is the gearbox (the flywheel and clutch are the engine's); a differential or a transfer case
group a mod adds goes in it too.
